In addition, more severe ice conditions this year increased the fuel consumption of the ferries.'

factual_claims.claim: Additionally, expenses for technical maintenance and repair of non-current assets rose by 80.0%, partly because the Group did not receive the insurance indemnity for icebreaker repairs that it had received in the prior year.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating expenses section states: 'Expenses related to technical maintenance and repair of non-current assets increased by EUR 1.2 million (+80.0%), as in the previous year the subsidiary OÜ TS Shipping received an insurance indemnity of EUR 0.9 million for repair works carried out following the technical incident involving the icebreaker Botnica in the summer of 2024.'

factual_claims.claim: Electricity costs also increased by 28.8% due to higher market prices, increased volumes, and a new security of supply fee.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating expenses section states: 'Electricity costs increased by EUR 0.7 million (+28.8%). The increase was driven by the new security of supply fee, higher electricity and network service prices and higher purchase volumes.'

factual_claims.claim: Depreciation, amortization, and impairment charges grew by 6.0% following the commissioning of new infrastructure and ferry dry-docking projects.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating expenses section states: 'Depreciation, amortisation and impairment increased by EUR 0.7 million (+6.0%). The increase was mainly attributable to the commissioning of the new quay at Paldiski South Harbour and the capitalisation of several ferry dry-docking projects.'

factual_claims.claim: Operational volumes reflected a challenging market environment.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management Report states: 'the increase in operating expenses... along with a decline in vessel calls and cargo volumes, had a negative impact on the Group’s financial performance.'

factual_claims.claim: Cargo volumes decreased by 5.0% to 6.5 million tonnes, with liquid bulk dropping significantly by 33.8% and dry bulk falling by 4.8%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating Volumes section states: 'In the first 6 months of 2026, the Group’s harbours handled a total of 6.5 million tonnes of cargo, a decrease of 0.3 million tonnes (–5.0%). The decline was mainly attributable to a decrease in liquid bulk volumes, which fell by 0.3 million tonnes (–33.8%). Dry bulk volumes also declined by 58 thousand tonnes (–4.8%).'

factual_claims.claim: This decline was attributed to the war in Ukraine affecting cargo flows and a search for alternative delivery routes by customers.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Main Economic Risks section states: 'Russia’s military activity in Ukraine has mainly affected the Group’s cargo business, resulting in a decreased share of liquid bulk. Liquid bulk cargo operators are looking for alternative cargo for delivery.'

factual_claims.claim: The number of vessel calls fell by 4.8%, and passenger numbers decreased by 2.0% to 3.6 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Key Performance Indicators table shows vessel calls decreased by 4.8% and passenger numbers decreased by 2.0% to 3,586 thousand.

factual_claims.claim: The passenger decline was largely concentrated on the Tallinn-Helsinki route, where traffic dropped by 2.6% due to the scheduled dry-docking of a competitor’s vessel and the absence of major music events that had boosted traffic in the previous year.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating Volumes section states: 'In the first 6 months of 2026, the number of passengers decreased by 73 thousand to 3.6 million (–2.0%). The largest decline was recorded on the Tallinn–Helsinki route, where passenger numbers fell by 85 thousand (–2.6%), mainly due to the scheduled dry-docking of Eckerö Line’s vessel Finlandia at the beginning of the year. By contrast, the number of cruise passengers increased... Due to an increase in the number of cruise ship calls... The number of passengers on the other routes remained broadly unchanged.' Further context in Q2 report mentions absence of music events.

factual_claims.claim: Conversely, cruise passenger numbers surged by 47.8% as the number of cruise ship calls increased.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating Volumes section states: 'By contrast, the number of cruise passengers increased by 32 thousand (+47.8%) as the number of cruise ship calls increased by 12 and the visiting ships had a higher combined passenger capacity.'

factual_claims.claim: Segment performance varied, with the Cargo harbours segment seeing the largest drop in adjusted EBITDA due to lower cargo volumes and the absence of one-off gains from land sales recorded in 2025.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Segment Reporting states: 'Adjusted EBITDA decreased in all segments in the first 6 months compared with the same period last year. The largest declines were recorded in the Cargo harbours segment (EUR –1.9 million)... The decrease in adjusted EBITDA was mainly attributable not only to lower revenue but also to lower other income (due to the disposal of land in Muuga Harbour in 2025)...'

factual_claims.claim: The Ferry segment also experienced a decline in adjusted EBITDA despite revenue growth, as rising fuel and personnel costs outweighed tariff indexation benefits.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Segment Reporting states: 'Adjusted EBITDA in the Ferry segment decreased despite higher revenue, as fuel costs increased due to both more severe ice conditions at the beginning of the year and significantly higher fuel prices. Personnel expenses also increased, partly due to the additional trips operated by the ferry Regula...'

factual_claims.claim: The Other segment saw revenue growth due to increased icebreaker utilization, though adjusted EBITDA fell due to higher repair costs.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Segment Reporting states: 'Revenue in segment Other increased by EUR 1.0 million in the first 6 months of the year, as the icebreaker Botnica commenced project-based work earlier... Adjusted EBITDA in segment Other decreased despite revenue growth because expenses related to the technical maintenance and repair of non-current assets increased. The increase in these expenses reflects... the more extensive repair works carried out this year on the hull and main engine of the icebreaker Botnica.'

factual_claims.claim: Net finance costs decreased by 11.2% due to lower debt levels.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Finance costs section states: 'Net finance costs decreased by EUR 0.3 million (–11.2%) in the first 6 months of the year due to lower interest expense on loans and borrowings resulting from the lower level of debt.'

factual_claims.claim: The Group maintained a stable dividend policy, paying EUR 19.2 million, equivalent to 85% of the previous year's profit.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Dividends section states: 'On 28 April 2026, the annual general meeting of shareholders approved the proposal of the management board to distribute a dividend of EUR 0.073 per share and EUR 19.2 million in total, i.e. in an amount equal to 85% of profit for the previous year.'

factual_claims.claim: Total assets decreased slightly to EUR 615.0 million, while net debt increased marginally to EUR 145.8 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Statement of Financial Position shows total assets of EUR 615,034 thousand (615.0 million) and net debt (loans less cash) of EUR 145,764 thousand (145.8 million).

factual_claims.claim: The company concluded the period with equity of EUR 367.7 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Statement of Changes in Equity shows total equity of EUR 367,677 thousand (367.7 million) at 30 June 2026.
